task.description: Implement the validated design at src/design/iss0612-provisioning-lock-scope-fix.md to fix ISS-0612/GH-556 in src/db/provisioning.zig's provisionTenantSchema(). This is a git-setup-already-done run (branch feature/WF03-GH556-20260807 exists and is checked out) -- do NOT run git-setup again, only implement + commit. Summary: restructure provisionTenantSchema() so a single lock_conn, acquired once via pool.acquire(), is reused across Step 2 (idempotency check), Steps 3-4 (bpm_provision_tenant_schema() SQL call), Step 6 (tenant_schemas timestamp update), and Step 6a (public.tenant promotion) -- removing each of those steps' own separate pool.acquire()/release() pairs. Lock acquire (acquireAdvisoryLock) happens once at the start on lock_conn; lock release (releaseAdvisoryLock) + pool.release(lock_conn) become a single defer pair registered once, covering every exit path including the idempotency fast-return. Step 5 (runForSchema migrations) is CONFIRMED BY CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to structurally require its own separate connection -- runForSchema's signature (src/db/migrations.zig ~line 104-116) takes (allocator, pool, migrations_dir, schema_name, force_reconcile), NOT a *Conn parameter, so it always calls pool.acquire() internally and cannot accidentally receive lock_conn. Do not change runForSchema's signature or attempt to pass lock_conn into it -- leave Step 5 exactly as it currently acquires its own connection. As defense-in-depth, also add a call to pg_advisory_unlock_all() in Pool.release() (src/db/pool.zig, after resetConnectionSearchPath around line 857, before the connection re-enters the idle set) so any future bug of this class becomes a harmless no-op instead of a silent hang. Read the full design doc before starting -- it has more precise detail than this summary.
acceptance_criteria: provisionTenantSchema() acquires lock_conn once and reuses it for Steps 2, 3-4, 6, 6a
Lock release + connection release happen via a single defer pair covering all exit paths
Step 5 (runForSchema) is unchanged in how it acquires its connection (stays separate, per the validated deadlock-freedom analysis)
Pool.release() defensively calls pg_advisory_unlock_all() before returning a connection to idle
zig build exits 0, no error-set output
The stress-test scenario from ISS-0612 (many concurrent same-tenant provisionTenantSchema calls) no longer stalls -- re-run a similar concurrent stress test and confirm all calls complete

result.summary: Fixed ISS-0612/GH-556: provisionTenantSchema() (src/db/provisioning.zig) previously acquired lock_conn, took the advisory lock, and released both within its own nested scope BEFORE Steps 2-6a began, so the lock serialized nothing. Restructured so lock_conn is acquired ONCE at function start and reused across Step 2 (idempotency check), Steps 3-4 (bpm_provision_tenant_schema() call), Step 6 (tenant_schemas timestamp update), and Step 6a (public.tenant promotion); a single defer pair (releaseAdvisoryLock then pool.release(lock_conn)) now covers every exit path including the idempotency fast-return. Step 5 (runForSchema) deliberately left unchanged -- it structurally cannot receive lock_conn (no *Conn parameter) and always acquires its own connection, per the validated design's deadlock-freedom analysis. Added defense-in-depth: Pool.release() (src/db/pool.zig) now calls pg_advisory_unlock_all() via a new clearConnectionAdvisoryLocks() helper, positioned after resetConnectionSearchPath and before the idle-set insertion, mirroring that function's mark-invalid-on-failure pattern. Discovered and fixed a blocking interaction: tests/unit/test_api08_auth.zig's ensureTenantDefaultSchema() (added by ISS-0209) wrapped its own outer acquireAdvisoryLock/releaseAdvisoryLock pair around its retry loop, relying on the pre-fix lock being a no-op. Once the lock genuinely spans Steps 2-6a, that outer wrapper self-deadlocked (its lock_conn held the lock while blocking on provisionTenantSchema(), whose own lock_conn blocked waiting for the outer lock to release) -- reproduced live via zig build test hanging with pg_stat_activity showing one idle connection holding the advisory lock and two others blocked waiting on it for 3+ minutes. Removed the now-redundant outer lock from ensureTenantDefaultSchema(); provisionTenantSchema()'s own lock now provides the check-then-act guarantee ISS-0209 needed, so the retry loop alone (unchanged backoff/escalation logic) is sufficient. Added a permanent regression test (tests/integration/iss0129_migration_run_advisory_lock_test.zig, 'ISS-0612: 12 threads x 8 rounds same-tenant concurrent provisionTenantSchema does not stall under pool_size=3') reproducing the original diagnosis's exact stress conditions. Concurrent stress-test result: BEFORE any fix, original defect stalled at 24/96 calls indefinitely (180s hard cap, PoolExhausted on force-termination, zero DB query activity during stall). AFTER the provisioning.zig fix alone (before the test-harness fix), zig build test hung again via a DIFFERENT mechanism (the ensureTenantDefaultSchema self-deadlock described above), confirmed live via pg_stat_activity/pg_locks showing a held-but-idle advisory lock blocking two waiters for 3+ minutes -- this was fixed by removing the outer lock from the test helper. AFTER both fixes: zig build test passes cleanly (939/1003 tests passed, 64 skipped -- identical to pre-change baseline, run twice for consistency), and the dedicated stress test completes 96/96 calls in ~2.2-2.3s with 0 non-retryable errors (verified in 2 consecutive runs). Per the validated design's own §3.2, pool_size=3 with 12 threads is below the 'minimum viable pool size of two connections per concurrently-provisioning tenant', so the stress test retries on PoolExhausted/MigrationFailed with bounded backoff rather than asserting zero contention -- Pool.acquire() fails fast (does not block/queue) by design, which is itself the intended improvement over the original silent indefinite hang.
